_role: Artifacts that deliberately live on a ref OTHER than the one you are reading, with the ref named. Read by check_artifacts ([K1]).
_why: [K1] exists because 41 artifacts were found living only on `modalities-cache`, 24 of them cited from the working branch, and the relative-link checker had caught one. Its message tells the reader to check whether the producing lane writes to a different ref before concluding the artifact was never run.

This file is where that answer goes once someone has checked. Without it the knowledge stays in prose, which is exactly the shape the systems model exists to remove -- and the document explaining the absence would itself trip the check that found it.

⛔ AN ENTRY HERE IS A CHECKED CLAIM, NOT A SILENCER. It must name the ref, the workflow that writes there, and why porting a copy would be WRONG rather than merely unnecessary. `not ported yet` is not a reason -- that is drift, and it belongs in the port, not here.

⚠ THE DEFAULT IS TO PORT. CLAUDE.md section 7 is explicit that a branch a workflow runs from must never be the only home of an artifact. This register is for the narrow case where a second copy would be actively harmful, not for the common case of not having got round to it.

elsewhere.written_by: research/modalities/vast_board_volatility.py, appended by the Vast price-sampling lane
elsewhere.why_not_ported: It is a LIVE APPEND-ONLY LOG -- one market sample per run, 3.9 MB and growing, its tip commit literally 'vast price sample <timestamp>'. A copy here would be stale the moment the next sample lands, which is the one-fact-one-home violation rather than a fix for one. Its only referrer on this branch is its own producer's `--out` default and the prose in systems/MIGRATION.md section 3.6 explaining this entry, so nothing cites it as evidence.
